text: Opened cold, API documentation can look overwhelming. Every good doc page answers the same three questions, though — find those first, and the rest is just detail.

This is a real, live documentation page, generated by Swagger UI — a tool that builds docs straight from an API's own specification. Look at the color coding: green for POST, orange for PUT, blue for GET. That convention shows up across most documentation tools, not just this one.

So here's what to look for, in order. Base URL and auth — where do requests go, and how do you prove who you are. Endpoints — what resources exist, and which methods work on each one. Required parameters — what you must send, versus what's optional.

Click into an endpoint and it spells everything out. Here, the status parameter is marked required, typed as an array of strings, sent as a query parameter, limited to three allowed values. Miss a required parameter, and that's one of the most common ways to earn yourself a 400 Bad Request.

Here's a completely different documentation site, built by a different tool — and it answers the exact same questions: required headers, each parameter's type, the valid values. Once you know what to look for, you can read almost any API's docs.
And that's the whole translation. Take the documented method, the URL, the required parameters — and you've got the real request Lesson 4 already taught you the anatomy of.
Base URL, endpoints, required parameters — that's how you read any API's docs. Chapter one is done. Next up, chapter two: the JSON that fills every one of those request and response bodies.
